source.quote: Grace Design's own page for the m908, read 2026-11-25. « sample rates of up to 192kHz / 24bit are supported. » - stated once for the device, with no per-connection breakdown and no spec table. Digital inputs: « Standard features include a total of 68 digital input channels via AES3, TOSLINK, S/PDIF, ADAT Lightpipe, and USB2. » and « 16 channel ADAT Lightpipe » as an input. Converter: no part is named; the page says only « Our latest generation AD / DA converters provide incredible dynamic range and resolution », with no D/A dynamic range or THD+N figure. Filtering: « 64-bit fixed-point filters for room correction and bass management ». No DSD figure appears anywhere.

facts.chip: Not named, and unlike the m900 and m905 this page gives no measurement either - only « Our latest generation AD / DA converters provide incredible dynamic range and resolution ».

_soixante_huit_canaux_dentree_numerique: « a total of 68 digital input channels via AES3, TOSLINK, S/PDIF, ADAT Lightpipe, and USB2 », with « 16 channel ADAT Lightpipe ». Sixty-eight channels on one device, and this catalogue's inputs model is built around a stereo pair per socket. Nothing is written per input: the page gives one rate for the whole device and a channel total that belongs to no particular interface.
_les_filtres_de_cette_page_sont_de_la_CO: « 64-bit fixed-point filters for room correction and bass management ». DSP the owner calibrates for a room, not the reconstruction filter device_settings records - the same distinction drawn on the Arcam SA45's « Dirac Live Room Correction ». No setting is written, and the arithmetic precision, 64-bit fixed point, is about the room filters and not about the conversion path.
